'''''Veronica stricta''''', [[Synonym (taxonomy)|synonym]] '''''Hebe stricta''''',<ref name=POWO_812694-1/> commonly called '''koromiko''', is a [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Plantaginaceae]], which is [[endemic (ecology)|endemic]] to New Zealand.

Koromiko is a [[Veronica sect. Hebe|hebe]] found throughout the Mainland New Zealand, with long pale green leaves and tiny white flowers in summer formed into a dense inflorescence longer than the leaves. It is a hardy plant and does not tolerate shade. It prefers full sun and open habitats on edge of bush and wetlands as it tolerates wet areas.{{citation needed|date=October 2022}}

''Veronica stricta'' is the most commonly referred to plant that is called koromiko.<ref name="MeaningTrees">{{cite q|Q118646408|pp=32-35}}</ref> 

==Taxonomy==
===Varieties===
{{As of|2022|October}}, [[Plants of the World Online]] accepted four varieties:<ref name=POWO_812694-1/>
* ''Veronica stricta'' var. ''egmontiana'' <small>(L.B.Moore) Garn.-Jones</small> – North Island
* ''Veronica stricta'' var. ''lata'' <small>(L.B.Moore) Garn.-Jones</small> – North Island
* ''Veronica stricta'' var. ''macroura'' <small>(Hook.f. ex Benth.) Garn.-Jones</small> – North Island
* ''Veronica stricta'' var. ''stricta'' – North and South Island

==Names==

The plant is typically referred to as koromiko in [[Māori language|Māori]]. Other regional names include kōkoromiko, koromuka, kōkoromuka and korohiko.<ref name="MeaningTrees"/> 

==Uses==

Koromiko is a commonly used plant in traditional [[Māori culture|Māori]] [[rongoā]] medicine, by chewing or boiling leaf buds, or applied in balms.<ref name="MeaningTrees"/> A sticky substance that is extruded from young leaf buds was traditionally mixed with blue pollen of ''[[Fuchsia excorticata]]'' for a form of make-up.<ref name="MeaningTrees"/> During the early European colonial era, koromiko leaves or extract was sold under names such as Monk's Herbal Extract as an [[antidiarrheal]] remedy.<ref name="MeaningTrees"/> 

Other traditional uses included lining [[hāngī]] to impart a flavour to cooked meat, and using the twigs for fires to cook [[moa]].<ref name="MeaningTrees"/> 

Koromiko is a pioneer plant useful to plant as a nurse crop for revegetation planting.{{citation needed|date=October 2022}}
